claims: The Artemis II mission is a roughly 10-day crewed test flight.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is aimed at sending four astronauts around the Moon and back.
The Artemis II mission uses the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Artemis II mission includes high-Earth orbit systems tests.
The Artemis II mission includes a three-day outbound transit.
The Artemis II mission includes a lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission includes a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
The Artemis II mission tests the Orion spacecraft’s life-support systems.
The SLS rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B in Florida.
The Artemis II launch is aimed for a 6:24 p.m. ET launch window.
After reaching orbit on Day 1 of the Artemis II mission, Orion separates from the upper stage.
On Day 1 of the Artemis II mission, the crew deploys solar arrays.
On Day 1 of the Artemis II mission, the crew performs a 90-minute check of systems.
On Days 1-2 of the Artemis II mission, Orion spends about a day in a high-Earth elliptical orbit.
The Artemis II mission includes a proximity operations demonstration where crew members manually fly the craft.
On Day 2 of the Artemis II mission, Orion's service module fires to send the spacecraft toward the Moon.
The Artemis II mission sets Orion on a figure-eight, free-return trajectory.
On Days 2-4 of the Artemis II mission, Orion spends roughly three days traveling to the Moon.
On Days 5-6 of the Artemis II mission, the crew swings around the Moon.
During the Artemis II lunar flyby, the crew passes thousands of miles beyond the Moon.
On Days 7-10 of the Artemis II mission, the spacecraft returns to Earth relying on Earth's gravity to guide its path back.
On Day 10 of the Artemis II mission, Orion reenters the atmosphere.
The Artemis II mission tests the heat shield during reentry.
On Day 10 of the Artemis II mission, Orion splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman (Commander), Victor Glover (Pilot), Christina Koch (Mission Specialist), and Jeremy Hansen (Mission Specialist).
The Artemis II spacecraft is the Orion capsule.
The objective of the Artemis II mission is to validate life-support systems and verify crew performance in deep space.
